definition: Following a single request as it travels through many different services.
exampleSentence: Distributed tracing showed that the slow checkout was caused by one service in the middle.

definition: The response time that 99 percent of requests are faster than.
exampleSentence: Average speed looks fine, but our p99 latency shows that some users wait over five seconds.

definition: The amount of failure a service is allowed to have while still meeting its target.
exampleSentence: We used up the whole error budget this month, so we paused new features to fix reliability.

definition: A group of ready-made threads that a program reuses to run tasks.
exampleSentence: The server became slow because every thread in the thread pool was waiting for the database.

definition: A set of open database connections that an application shares and reuses.
exampleSentence: We increased the connection pool size because requests were waiting for a free connection.

definition: A chart that shows which functions use the most time in a program.
exampleSentence: The flame graph showed that most of the time was spent in one image resizing function.

definition: Testing how a system behaves under the number of users it is expected to have.
exampleSentence: Load testing showed that the website stays fast with up to five thousand visitors.

definition: Pushing a system beyond its normal limits to find out when and how it breaks.
exampleSentence: Stress testing revealed that the server crashes when memory use reaches ninety-five percent.

definition: Handling more load by adding more servers instead of making one server bigger.
exampleSentence: Horizontal scaling lets us add two more web servers before the big sale starts.

definition: Handling more load by giving one server more CPU and memory.
exampleSentence: Vertical scaling was the quick fix, but a single bigger server is still a single point of failure.

definition: Automatically adding or removing servers depending on the current load.
exampleSentence: Autoscaling added six servers during the campaign and removed them again at night.

definition: The extra delay when a service or function starts after being idle.
exampleSentence: The first request after midnight is slow because of the cold start of the serverless function.

definition: The automatic process that frees memory that a program no longer uses.
exampleSentence: Long pauses from garbage collection made the app freeze for a second every few minutes.

definition: A platform that runs, scales and manages containers across many servers.
exampleSentence: Kubernetes restarts the failed container automatically, so the service stays online.

definition: A package of templates that describes how to install an application on Kubernetes.
exampleSentence: We install the whole monitoring tool on the cluster with a single Helm chart.

definition: Running two identical environments and switching traffic to the new one when it is ready.
exampleSentence: With a blue-green deployment, we can go back to the old version in seconds if something fails.

definition: Giving a new version to a small group of users first to check for problems.
exampleSentence: The canary release reached five percent of users, and we watched the error rate before continuing.

definition: A way of working where developers merge small changes into the main branch very often.
exampleSentence: Trunk-based development means we avoid long branches and merge conflicts.

definition: Managing infrastructure by keeping its desired state in Git and applying changes automatically.
exampleSentence: With GitOps, a pull request is the only way to change the production setup.

definition: Servers are never changed after creation; you replace them with new ones instead.
exampleSentence: Immutable infrastructure means we never patch a running server but deploy a fresh one.

definition: Keeping development, test and production environments as similar as possible.
exampleSentence: Environment parity helps us avoid bugs that appear only in production.

definition: Storing and controlling passwords, keys and tokens safely instead of putting them in code.
exampleSentence: Secret management tools rotate the database password every month without any developer seeing it.

definition: Testing that two services still agree on the format of the messages they exchange.
exampleSentence: Contract testing caught the breaking change before the new API version reached production.

definition: Testing that a rule always holds by trying many automatically generated inputs.
exampleSentence: Property-based testing found a bug that only appeared with very long names.

definition: Making small changes to the code to check whether the tests notice them.
exampleSentence: Mutation testing showed that our tests still passed when we broke an important condition.

definition: A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any change to the code.
exampleSentence: One flaky test keeps failing the pipeline, so the team no longer trusts the results.

definition: A fake object used in a test in place of a real dependency.
exampleSentence: We used a test double for the email service so the test does not send real emails.

definition: Deliberately causing failures in a system to learn whether it can survive them.
exampleSentence: Chaos engineering helped us discover that the app crashes when one database node disappears.

definition: A quick, basic test that checks whether the most important functions work.
exampleSentence: After every deployment, a smoke test checks that the login page and the API respond.

definition: Moving testing and quality checks to earlier steps of the development process.
exampleSentence: Shift-left testing means developers run security checks on their own laptops before committing.

definition: Automatically checking source code for problems without running it.
exampleSentence: Static analysis warned us about an unused variable and a possible null reference.

definition: A sign in the code that may point to a deeper design problem.
exampleSentence: A method with two hundred lines is a clear code smell and should be split up.

definition: A number that shows how many different paths exist through a piece of code.
exampleSentence: The function has a cyclomatic complexity of thirty, so it is too hard to test.

definition: The extra effort you pay later because of quick, poor solutions taken earlier.
exampleSentence: Every new feature takes longer because of technical debt interest from old shortcuts.

definition: Checking that the data a user sends is in the expected and safe format.
exampleSentence: Input validation rejects any phone number that contains letters before it reaches the database.

definition: Removing or escaping dangerous characters from data before it is used.
exampleSentence: Sanitization removes script tags from comments so they cannot run in other users' browsers.

definition: Turning data into a fixed-length code that cannot easily be reversed.
exampleSentence: Hashing is used to store passwords so that even admins cannot read them.

definition: Adding random data to a password before hashing it, so equal passwords have different hashes.
exampleSentence: Salting makes it much harder for attackers to crack many passwords at once.

definition: An attack that targets a supplier or a software library to reach many victims.
exampleSentence: The supply chain attack spread through a popular library that thousands of projects had installed.

definition: Thinking through who might attack a system and how, before it is built.
exampleSentence: We ran a threat modeling workshop before building the new payment feature.
